why: DeviceCapabilitiesSchema is strict, so a capability with no field there is one a device physically cannot tell the server about. Ten of the fourteen capabilities a machine has and a browser does not are in that position today. Each is recorded with the reason and the owner who closes it; closing one without moving it into "advertises" fails, so this file cannot become a list of things nobody intends to fix.

canUseWorkingDirectory.why: A device that has opened a folder and one that has not are the same row to the server, so a task that needs a checkout cannot be offered to the right machine.

canUseFileSystem.why: The checklist requires filesystem access in the advertisement and the schema has no field for it. A server routing a file-writing task has to assume it from the surface name.

canRunLocalCode.why: Whether this build may run a local program is a policy answer as much as a platform one, and the heartbeat carries neither, so a hook or a skill is offered to a device that will refuse it.

canUseTerminal.why: A terminal is the capability a code session most depends on and the one the heartbeat is most often asked about, and it is not there.

canUseLocalDatabase.why: The desktop keeps a local store the cloud can hand work to; nothing on the wire says a given device has one.

canTakeScreenshot.why: Screen capture is granted per operating system and can be refused after install, so it is exactly the kind of answer that cannot be inferred from the surface name.

canUseClipboard.why: Reading the clipboard is a separate permission on every platform and the heartbeat has no field for it.

canUseNativeIntegrations.why: Native integrations differ by operating system and by install, so a single boolean derived from the surface is wrong for most devices.

canUsePhotos.why: The photo library is a mobile permission the user grants or refuses after install, and the heartbeat reports neither.

canUseNotifications.why: A device that cannot show a notification still reads as notifiable, so a completed run is announced to a machine that will not show it.
